assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall state opened a new paradigm of topological band theory with a clear theoretical prediction, a decisive experimental realization in HgTe, and broad impact across condensed matter, photonics and quantum-device ideas. Originality and lasting influence are exceptional.
assessment.attribution: Kane (with Mele) supplied the Z2 theory and Molenkamp's group, following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal, observed the quantum spin Hall edge transport. The credited names support a Kane-Molenkamp pairing; Xue's quantum anomalous Hall realization is a distinct, later step, and Mele, Zhang, Hasan and others in this area are outside this entry's credited names or belong to the overlapping B045, so the allocation is genuinely contested.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed for 15+ years in many materials and laboratories; the interpretation is stable and the field is mature. Recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Credit is split across theory proposers, the HgTe experiment, 3D topological insulators and the QAH effect; any two- or three-person prize leaves out major contributors.
I rely on my own background knowledge of the priority history and have not verified it independently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED brought strong light-matter coupling to superconducting circuits and underpins dispersive readout, qubit coupling and most present superconducting quantum processors. It is a clear, original and highly consequential concept that turned a laboratory curiosity into a platform for quantum computing.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Wallraff and Schoelkopf (with Girvin, Huang, Majer and Devoret's group as important co-authors) are the central names for the 2004 proposal and experiment. The three credited names form a coherent configuration, though the broader credit tree is wider.
assessment.maturity: Thoroughly confirmed and reproduced worldwide for two decades. Timing is subtle because the 2025 prize already recognised macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits; a close successor in the same ecosystem may be seen as premature repetition. I work in this area and direct WACQT, which I would disclose as a potential bias in either direction.
uncertainties: Closeness to the 2025 prize may argue for waiting.
My own field proximity and Chalmers links to the circuit-QED community could colour my judgement; I treat this as a disclosed bias rather than evidence.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atomic quantum information processing, from the Cirac-Zoller trapped-ion gate proposal to ion and neutral-atom quantum simulation, defined a founding architecture for quantum computing and is deeply influential across AMO physics. The ideas are original and have been realised experimentally at high fidelity.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller made the decisive theoretical proposal and Blatt (alongside Wineland, who already shared the 2012 prize, and Monroe, Wineland-NIST colleagues, who are not credited here) led key experimental realisations. The Cirac-Zoller-Blatt triple is plausible but leaves out other experimental pioneers such as Monroe and Wineland-group contributors, so fairness depends on framing.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature with extensive independent confirmation and commercial-scale trapped-ion processors. Timely, although the 2012 prize overlaps conceptually.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 Haroche-Wineland prize and with B033 and B047 (identical or near-identical credited names) means the discovery framing would need to be narrowed.
Credit for the experimental gate demonstrations is distributed beyond the three names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum error correction, including Shor's code and Steane's CSS codes plus Kitaev's topological codes and fault-tolerance ideas, is the theoretical foundation that makes scalable quantum computing possible in principle. The concept is original and consequential, and experimental demonstrations of below-threshold operation are now appearing.
assessment.attribution: Shor, Steane and Kitaev are central, with Calderbank, Gottesman, Knill, Laflamme and others also decisive; the credited three form a defensible but incomplete configuration. Shor's algorithm is a separate contribution, and the allocation between code construction, fault-tolerance theorems and topological codes is not cleanly resolved.
assessment.maturity: Theory is stable and now getting experimental validation in superconducting and ion platforms, but full fault-tolerant demonstration is still evolving; recognition is slightly early on the experimental side yet mature as theory.
uncertainties: Rich priority disputes (Shor vs Steane vs Calderbank-Shor-Steane, Gottesman, Knill-Laflamme).
Experimental error correction is not yet at the scale that would make the practical impact settled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal, achieve unprecedented precision and stability, enable tests of fundamental physics and relativistic geodesy, and prepare the redefinition of the second. Clear, original, high-impact precision measurement.
assessment.attribution: Katori conceived the magic-wavelength lattice clock; Ye's group drove record accuracy and many-body clock physics. A two-person prize is clean and well supported by the credited names, although other contributors (e.g. Lemonde, Derevianko, Hollberg, Hall's frequency-comb work already recognised in 2005) shaped related steps.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by multiple national laboratories with agreeing comparisons; the redefinition of the second is pending, which would strengthen the case.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2005 prize for frequency-comb and precision spectroscopy.
Some uncertainty about the extent of independent credit for ytterbium and strontium implementations.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Baryon acoustic oscillations provide a standard ruler for cosmology and were detected in SDSS and 2dFGRS galaxy clustering, anchoring dark energy and Hubble-constant constraints. Impact on precision cosmology is deep and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Eisenstein's SDSS luminous-red-galaxy detection and the 2dFGRS analysis led by Cole and Peacock (with the large collaborations behind them) were simultaneous independent detections, which fits the credited three. Collaboration-scale work complicates individual attribution, and the original theoretical idea belongs to earlier CMB-era workers outside these names.
assessment.maturity: Many independent confirmations (BOSS, eBOSS, DESI) over twenty years; mature, though recent DESI results hint at dynamical dark energy and keep interpretation evolving.
uncertainties: Large-collaboration origins make a small laureate set an imperfect representation of the discovery.
The theoretical origin of the BAO standard ruler is outside the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene linked a striking theoretical prediction of flat bands to the discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity, and launched twistronics. Highly original and fast-moving with broad impact on quantum materials.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the flat-band prediction and Jarillo-Herrero's group delivered the decisive 2018 experiments; the credited trio is a coherent theory-plus-experiment configuration, though the Cao-Fatemi-Jarillo-Herrero co-authors and the Dean, Young, Yacoby and Kim groups also contributed substantially.
assessment.maturity: Widely reproduced, but the nature of the superconductivity and the correlated states is still debated, so the interpretation is not yet stable and recognition is somewhat early.
uncertainties: Possible premature recognition relative to maturing alternatives.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Semiconductor quantum-dot spin qubits, from the Loss-DiVincenzo proposal to single-spin control and silicon qubits, give a scalable, CMOS-compatible route to quantum processors. Original and consequential, and close to my own mesoscopic background.
assessment.attribution: Loss (with DiVincenzo, who is not credited here) proposed the scheme; Tarucha, Vandersypen and Marcus carried out foundational experiments. The credited Loss-Vandersypen-Tarucha configuration is defensible, but omitting Marcus and DiVincenzo is a contested allocation.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced across many groups with high-fidelity two-qubit gates in silicon; the platform is still competing with other qubit technologies and scalability is unproven, so maturity is moderate.
uncertainties: Eventual platform winner is unknown, affecting how lasting the impact will appear.
Credit split between theory proposal and several pioneering experimental groups.
